title: Investigate cudaMallocAsync hoarding during continuous KV-prefetch with mixed-length requests
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Intermittent GPU memory growth observed on dedicated pools when continuous batching is enabled together with aggressive KV cache prefetching. Symptoms: long tail of 'reserved' memory that never returns to the pool, elevated cudamallocasync backlog visible on sampling, occasional OOMs under mixed short/long sequence workloads. This ticket scopes a root-cause investigation and short/medium-term mitigations.
steps_to_reproduce: Start dedicated edge pool with 4x A100 and enable continuous batching (batcher window=50ms) and KV prefetch=on
Run mixed workload: 60% short sequences (<=64 tokens) and 40% long sequences (>=2048 tokens) arriving with Poisson interarrival that creates overlapping batching windows
Monitor GPU usage via nvidia-smi, cudamem logs, and our allocator telemetry (async_free_backlog, slab_resident_bytes) for 30 minutes
Trigger synthetic high-concurrency client to saturate the batcher while toggling KV prefetch frequency (normal, aggressive)
Observe memory not returning between long-sequence requests and see increase in async_free_backlog and pinned staging resident counters
investigation_summary: We reproduced the leak pattern on a local perf cluster. Early traces show allocations for KV prefetch pages pinned on streams that outlive the request due to cudaFreeAsync being deferred until stream sync points which are delayed by continuous batching merge windows. The pool's slab hysteresis and LRU eviction are preventing immediate reuse because allocations remain resident in a different stream context. Kernel selection / stream affinity changes for long sequences cause cross-stream CUDA events to postpone actual frees leading to accumulation. There is also evidence of small size-class fragmentation from mixed short/long workloads which increases slab count and reduces reclamation efficiency.
hypotheses: H1: cudaFreeAsync semantics + stream-affinity cause delayed physical frees when prefetch allocations are posted to streams that don't reach their sync point quickly under continuous batching
H2: Allocator slab hysteresis thresholds are too conservative for mixed-length workloads, keeping many small slabs resident and preventing reuse for larger long-sequence allocations
H3: KV prefetching aggressiveness creates many short-lived allocations on non-main streams which are held until batch merge completes, magnifying fragmentation and increasing total resident memory
experiments_run: Disable KV prefetch: memory returns to baseline, async_free_backlog falls — correlates with H3
Force cudaDeviceSynchronize at request end (instrumented): frees occur immediately but latency penalty unacceptable — validates H1
Reduced slab_hysteresis from 20% to 5%: lowered resident slabs after long-run but increased churn and slight latency jitter — partial mitigation of H2
Pinned prefetch to main worker stream (instead of per-request stream): reduced async_free_backlog and improved reuse in allocator sampling
findings: Root cause is multi-factor: combination of cudaMallocAsync/freeAsync stream behavior, continuous-batcher-induced delay of stream sync points, and allocator hysteresis thresholds tuned for stable homogeneous workloads not mixed-length traffic
Aggressive KV prefetching amplifies the issue by creating many allocations on streams that do not synchronize frequently under batching windows
Immediate full sync fixes memory but is unacceptable for latency; allocator tuning and stream-affinity changes give better cost/latency tradeoffs
There is measurable fragmentation: small-size slabs dominate resident pages in mixed workloads which reduces allocator's ability to satisfy large linear KV allocations without new slabs
proposed_actions: Short-term (low-risk): Pin KV prefetch allocations to a dedicated prefetch stream with periodic controlled synchronization to allow timely freeAsync without blocking request-critical streams (rollout: canary then fleet)
Short-term (config): Expose KV prefetch aggressiveness toggle and default to conservative in Dedicated pools until mitigation is deployed
Medium-term (allocator changes): Reduce slab hysteresis for mixed-size workloads and introduce cross-size compaction passes during low-util windows to defragment resident slabs
Medium-term (runtime): Add async_free_backlog monitoring alert and auto-throttle KV prefetch when backlog > threshold
Long-term (research): Evaluate stream-agnostic deferred-free queue in runtime that coalesces frees without requiring device-wide sync and cooperates with cudaMallocAsync semantics
Follow-up: Write benchmark to emulate mixed traffic and run nightly to catch regressions
risks_and_tradeoffs: Pinning prefetch allocations to a shared stream reduces backlog but may increase contention; must validate latency under 99th percentile
Lowering hysteresis increases allocation churn and potential fragmentation elsewhere — needs controlled Canary and cost monitoring
Any solution that schedules additional synchronizations risks latency regression; balance by using background syncs or opportunistic compaction
Disabling aggressive prefetching reduces throughput for cache-miss heavy workloads — document for customers and provide toggle
next_steps: Implement prefetch-to-dedicated-stream prototype (ENG-87921-branch) and run canary on two Dedicated pools: pool-ded-nyc-7 and pool-ded-sfo-3
Add async_free_backlog + slab_resident_bytes widgets to Console per-pool dashboard and create alert (SLO: backlog<256MB sustained)
Create a test harness to simulate mixed short/long sequence traffic for CI regression (owner: Liam)
Schedule design review with Runtime and Serving teams to align on compaction API and telemetry metrics (meeting: 2026-03-16)
Update docs: add known-issue note to Dedicated release notes for runtime-2.3
